full_judgment:
"Let a Rule Nisi be issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the impugned Election schedule dated 29-4-2016 for holding Election of No. 11 Juidandi Union Parishad under Upazila-Anowara, District-Chittagong issued by the respondent No. 7 (Annexure-J2 ) shall not be declared to have been issued without lawful authority and is of no legal effect And as to why the respondent No.2 shall not be directed to complete the process of delimitation of the No.11 Juidandi Union Parishad under Upazila-Anowara, District-Chittagong and to publish fresh Voter list of No. 11 Juidandi Union Parishad under Upazila-Anowara, District-Chittagong and/or pass such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper. " 

 3. Writ Petition No. 2424 of 2016 has been filed by Mohammad Ayub Ali and Kafil Uddin and Rule Nisi was issued in this writ petition, in the following terms: "Let a Rule Nisi be issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the inaction of the respondents in not taking necessary initiatives to determine boundaries and to prepare up to date voter list of Ward No. 2, 3 and 4 under No. 11 Juidandi Union Parishad, Anawara Upazila, Chittagong shall not be declared illegal and/or pass such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper." 

 6. There were 50% of the area of each wards bearing No. 1-4 of the No.11 Juidandi Union Parishad, Anowara, Chattogram had been disappeared by erosion/diluvion and the same re-appeared at the opposite side of the Sangu River which divided the Boilgaon Mouza, Bashkhali and wards No. 1-4 of the No.11 Juidandi Union Parishad under Anowara Upazila. For the erosion and alluvion, the respondents in the meantime published a Gazette Notification dated 13-7-1994 with regard to right, title and interest of the inhabitants of the river side and the right title and interest of the original tenant or his successor in interest which subsists in the lands of a holding or portion thereof during the period of loss by diluvion if such land re-appear in situ within thirty years of their loss. 

 7. By the said erosion/diluvian the respondents did not meddle to the said Gazette Notification and by ignoring all the dis-appearances of the lands they prepared voter list and by the said wrong voter list, the respondents conducted the previous elections. But in the present circumstances and since the Government published the amended Local Government (Union Parishad) Ain, 2009 and as per sections 13 and 17 of the said Ain, the respondents are bound to determine the local areas of the union parishad and its wards. In this particular area, since there were so many reasons behind both the Upazilas, in such situation the respondents are bound to demarcate the area of the Wards No. 1-4 of the No. 11 Juidandi Union Parishad with Boilgaon Mouza, Banshkhali. 

 10. By filing a supplementary affidavit today, the petitioner further states that due to bonafide mistake the petitioner could not mention his official position in the writ petition. Further, the petitioner submitted application to the Secretary, Local Government, Rural Development and Cooperatives and separately to the Chief Election Commissioner, both on 18-7-2016 informing about erosion of lands in several wards of his union parishad and both the applications were received by their offices on 19-7-2016 and 18-7-2016 respectively. The Upazila Nirbahi Officer, Anowara, Chattogram by his memo dated 10-7-2016 forwarded a reconstruction plan submitted to him for Shadhonpur Union Parishad and Juidandi Union Parishad to the Deputy Commissioner, Chattogram. The Election Commission Secretariat by their memo dated 28-2-2016 informed that after reconstruction of the wards by Ministry of LGRD, the voter list shall be corrected. 

 11. In writ petition No. 2424 of 2016 the petitioners state that they are permanent residents and registered voters of village Juidandi, ward No. 01 and 04 respectively under No. 11 Juidandi Union Parishad, Anowara Upazila, District-Chattogram. 40% area of ward No.01 has been disappeared due to erosion caused by the Sangu river. The respondents without determining the boundaries of wards No. 1-4 and without preparing up-to-date voter list, are trying to hold election of the No.11 Juidandi Union Parishad election illegally and arbitrary without due process of law and hence the right of the petitioners to exercise their franchise as voters of the said union parishad has been affected. The petitioners and others are continuously submitting applications to the authority concern for determination of area of two Union Parishads, namely, No.2 Sadanpur Union Parishad, Banshkhali and No.11 Juidandi Union Parishad, Anowara. One Abdus Sukur and others also filed an application to the Assistant Commissioner (Land) Banshkhali to demarcate the area by appointing a Government Surveyor and to install pacca pillar on the northern and southern side. The application was registered as Da. 378 dated 28-12-2015. Pursuant to said application the Upazila land Office, Banshkhali issued a notice upon both the parties as mentioned in the said application asking them to appear on 24-2-2016 and to be present in the investigation and measurement. 

 12. Upon application of the local people of both union parishads, the local administration took step to determine the area and in this regard the Upazila Nirbahi Officer, Banshkhali issued a memo on 27-12-1987 addressing Upazila Nirbahi Officer, Anowara, Chattogram requesting him to fix a date for installation of boundary pillar. But after long period of time those initiatives have not been materialized and the matter is still pending. Since earlier initiatives of local administration were not materialized, the writ petitioners filed two separate applications to the Deputy Commissioner, Chattogram and the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Chattogram requesting them to take necessary step to settle the boundary dispute between two union parishads with a reference to the earlier memo dated 27-12-1987 and 12-11-1987. But they did not respond in any manner. The Chairman of No. 2 Sadhanpur Union Parishad under Banshkhali Upazila, also filed an application on 5-4-2011 to the respondent No. 7, the Chief Eleciton Officer, Chattogram for upholding the previous area of Banshkhali Upazila, Mouza Boilgaon and Kharda Mozaffarabad. The petitioners and others submitted applications on 1-2-2016, 16-2-2016 and 17-2-2016 before the respondents requesting to determine boundaries of the wards as well as to prepare up-to-date correct voter list of No. 11 Juidandi Union Parishad for proper and effective election. It has been stated in the applications that the wards have been merged with the Sangu river due to river erosion and people of the wards have gone in other wards due to which their names have not been enlisted in the voter list and similar application was filed before Election Commissioner on 16-2-2016. 

 13. The respondents are trying to hold election without demarcating boundaries of the wards as well as preparing up to date voter list with an ulterior motive in violation of sections 13 and 17 of the Local Government (Union Parishad) Act, 2009. 

 14. If the election of the Union is held without demarcating the boundaries of the wards without fresh voter list, the people including the petitioners would not be able to exercise their voting right and, as such, an order may be passed directing the respondents to prepare fresh voter list by demarcating the area of concern Union Parishad. 

 16. By filing a supplementary affidavit today the petitioner further states that the Upazila Nirbahi Officer, Anowara, Chattogram by his memo dated 10-7-2016 forwarded a reconstruction plan of the union parishad to the Deputy Commissioner, Chattogram which was submitted to him by the Sadhanpur Union Parishad and the Juidandi Union Parishad. The Chairman of the Juidandi Union Parishad submitted application to the Secretary, Local Government, Rural Development and Co-operative on 18-7-2016 informing him about erosion of several wards of his union parishad and it was received on 19-7-2016. He also informed officially to the Chief Election Commissioner about river erosion of several wards of No.11 Juidandi Union Parishad and the same was received on 18-7-2016. The Assistant Commissioner (Land), Anowara, Chattogram by his memo dated 14-12-2016 forwarded a report to the Upazila Nirbahi Officer, Anowara, Chattogram for reconstruction of Sadhanpur Union Parishad and Juidandi Union Parishad and in return the Upazila Nirbahi Officer, Anowara, Chattogram forwarded the same to the Deputy Com-missioner, Chattogram by his memo dated 14-12-2016 concurring reconstruction of Sadhanpur Union Parishad and Juidandi Union Parishad. 

 17. In writ petition No. 5341 of 2016, the added respondent No. 11 did not file an affidavit in opposition. However, by filing an application for discharging the Rule the respondent states that the dispute arose between two unions i.e shadhanpur union and Juidandi union but in the meantime election of No.2 Sadhanpur Union Parishad was completed and the election result was published through Bangladesh Gazette on 16-5-2017. The writ petitioner was the elected Chairman of the said Juidandi Union Parishad for the tenure 2011 to 2016 and during his tenure he did not raise the issue regarding demarcation or take any step for demarcation. After completion of the tenure of Chairman-ship, in order to continue in the office of Chairman, with a false plea the petitioner filed this writ petitioner after declaration of election schedule and obtaining the order of stay from this Court, kept the applicant outside from the election. It is further stated that none of the local people raised objection against the draft voter list and the final voter list was published on 31-1-2016. The writ petitioner, even did not offer his candidature in the election. 

 18. The added respondent No.12 by filing an application for discharging the Rule and supplementary affidavit thereto in writ petition No. 5341 of 2016 states that at the time of filing the writ petition, the petitioner was a sitting chairman of Juidandi Union Parishad. But the petitioner did not disclose his identity in the instant writ petition. Rather he filed the writ petition under the guise of public interest litigation and obtained the Rule by suppressing the aforesaid relevant facts. The writ petitioner does not qualify the criterion to file the public interest litigation before the High Court Division in accordance with the principles set up in the case of 18 BLC (AD) 116 and, as such, the instant writ is not maintainable. 

 22. Mr ABM Altaf Hossain, the learned Advocate appearing for the added respondent No 12 contends that this respondent is a prospective candidate for the post of Chairman in the present union parishad election scheduled to be held in the year 2016 and that just after pronouncement of election schedule, the writ petitioner of writ petition No. 5341 of 2016 filed the writ petition on plea of defect voter list and delimitation of the area of Union in order to postpone the election and thereby to enjoy his office of Chairman beyond the statutory tenure. He also contends that inspite of being sitting chairman the writ petitioner deliberately suppressed his identity and describing him as a prospective candidate, filed the writ petition. As such, the Rule is liable to be discharged with cost for suppression of material facts. He again contends that in the case of Khalilur Rnhmand (Md) vs Government of Bangladesh and others reported in 52 DLR (AD) 115 and the case of Nekbar Ali vs Government of Bangladesh and others reported in 6 ADC 246, the apex Court have settled the ratio that sitting Chairman should not challenge the action or non action, regarding the delimitation of union parishad and that the delimitation process being policy matter involving disputed question of facts, should not be entertained under the writ jurisdiction. Knowing fully about the said ratio, the petitioner deliberately suppressed his identity as a Chairman. 

 27. In view of above, it is apparent that after pronouncement of the election schedule, all of a sudden the petitioner came before the Court with this writ petition seeking direction to complete the process of delimitation of the Union alongwith fresh voter list with a malafide intention for postponing the election in order to continue his office as Chairman beyond the statutory tenure which was 2011-2016. 

 28. Secondly, we have gone through the cited case reported in 52 DLR (AD) 115 wherein the apex Court held as under: 

 “……… In the instant case the petitioner is a Chairman of the Pourashava and because of the impugned Gazette Notification relating to delimitation of wards he cannot be said to be an aggrieved person within the meaning for Article 102 of the Constitution in that by such Notification no right of his either constitutional or legal has been infringed." 

 29. We have also carefully gone through the cited case reported in 6 ADC page 246 wherein our apex Court held as under: 

 "It appears from the record that the determination of the boundary of the Municipality or political unit is an administrative act of the writ respondent under Pourashava Ordinance, 1977 and it is obviously a policy matter, as such the writ petitioner has no locus standi to file the writ petition. In case of Nizamuddin and others vs Bangladesh, the Appellate Division held that alteration of boundary of the Municipality is a question of fact which cannot be decided in writ jurisdiction. The similar question was decided by the Appellate Division in the case reported in 5 BLC (AD) 150 that the requirement of population is also a question of fact which could not be disturbed by the High Court Division and accordingly discharged the Rules as not maintainable." 

 33. From writ petition No. 2424 of 2016 and other materials available in both writ petitions and the submissions of the learned Advocates for the petitioners of both the writ petitions, it appears that the petitioners allege certain portions of wards No.1-4 of Juidandi Union have been disappeared due to erosion of river Sangu and at the same time, certain areas have also been reappeared by alluvion under the said union. In this situation, question arises whether section 17 of the Act, 2009 will come into play here. 

 40. In Writ Petition No. 2424 of 2016 the petitioners have challenged inaction of the respondents in taking initiatives for determination of boundaries of Union and also for preparing upto date voter list of wards No. 2-4 of Juidandi Union. 

 41. The writ petitioners' prayer or the applications (filed by other people) as annexed to the writ petitions do not reflect that they ever prayed for reconstruction of Union Parishad. Their applications only sought delimitation of boundary of certain wards. Even the other correspondences of the respondents and both the writ petitions do not seek reconstruction of Union and that the Rules Nisi were also not issued regarding reconstruction of the Juidandi Union. All the previous relevant papers and the writ petitions are relating to boundary determination, delimitation and voter list. Therefore, the plea of reconstruction of Union Parishad is an after thought plea which was never the case of petitioners. Further, as we observed above that there is no such situation for reconstruction of said Union in accordance with section 17 of the Act, 2009. 

 42. Therefore, we are of the view that the election of Juidandi Union Parishad should not be postponed or stopped, just due to erosion of some portions of certain wards. Moreover, we find that the election of other union parishad, namely, Sadhanpur Union Parishad has already been held. 

 43. From 2016, the election process is totally stopped at the instance of petitioners and that the petitioner of writ petition No. 5341 of 2016 is enjoying the office of chairman for long 11 years without any election. During his valid tenure of 5 years he did never utter a single word raising cause of delimitation or reconstruction. At the eve of his tenure, just before declaration of election schedule, the petitioners of writ petition No. 2424 of 2016 filed the writ petition to postpone the election process by interim prayer raising plea of determination of boundaries of union and fresh voter list. But they failed to get interim order although Rule Nisi was issued. Subsequently, just after declaration of election schedule, the sitting Chairman came to the Court by filing writ petition No. 5341 of 2016 for postponing election on the ground of delimitation by suppressing his identity as Chairman. Thus, it is apparent that the petitioners have not come with clean hands before the Court to seek such equitable relief.
